doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: Ben Casey, Mister Roberts and the Andy Williams show
summary: Mandel recalls TV episodes and the live Andy Williams variety show where he met Dave Grusin and joked with Williams's perfect ears.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So, for television you did something, I remember seeing some Ben Casey episodes…
Yeah, I did.
How many of those did you do, quite a few?
Oh, I don't know, I don’t know, I just never took count of those things.
And what else, Mister Roberts?

Yeah, I did that. I didn't do much, I think I subbed for Frank Perkins a few times while he was ill, he was having an operation of some kind, but that was his show. He's the guy who wrote, “Stars Fell on Alabama.”
Ah-ha.
Yeah.
Yeah and you did some things for Andy Williams’ variety show right?

Oh yeah, in fact Dave Grusin and I, that's where we met and became very close buddies, we were on Andy’s show for a couple years. That was a fun show to do ‘cause you know it was live TV, we had a good band.
And a lot of music.

And a lot of music and Andy was a wonderful musician and singer, you know, this is one guy who has probably the best ears of anyone around, probably from all those years of singing hard parts for Kay Thompson. He has laser ears, I used to make a game of trying to throw him with modulations and I never succeeded. I’d write impossible, outrageous things you wouldn't do to a singer, not for a singer to a singer is really…
[laughs]
And he’d never crack a smile, he’d just, he’d never flinch, you know, he’d just do it [laughs] because he knew I was doing a number with him. In fact I don’t think we ever talked about it.
Well, Dave…
Sort of a little like that, did you read the – well I won't mention that on this tape ‘cause it’s really not germane. Did you read Oscar Peterson’s biography [The Will to Swing] that Gene Lees wrote?
Yes.
You remember that scene when Ray Brown and Herb Ellis dyed their hair to each other's color and Oscar Peterson would never acknowledge that he noticed it.
[laughs]
In all the years there've known him since.
[They both laugh]
This was sort of one of those kind of things.
Dave Grusin was Andy’s musical director at the time, right?
Yes he was, no, first he was his piano player. I got knocked out the first time I ever heard him play, I said, “Good, God, what’s this, something new.”
